vector.answer: Across the retrieved LERs, several different HPCI (and closely related) components have failed. At Quad Cities (LER 366-2024-001-00), the HPCI outboard steam isolation valve received a spurious close signal due to age-related failure of an RCIC Analog Transmitter Trip System (ATTS) card, whose electronic noise affected the adjacent HPCI ATTS card. At a plant reporting LER 237-2025-003-00, HPCI was rendered inoperable by a damaged stop valve closed-indicating light socket and an opened negative 125 VDC fuse, triggered when the HPCI Turbine Turning Gear engaged unexpectedly. At Quad Cities Unit 1 (LER 254-2022-001-00), HPCI was declared inoperable during a surveillance, with alarms received for the HPCI Gland Exhauster and associated component failures listed as a limit switch (LS) and a relay (RLY). At Edwin I. Hatch Unit 1 (LER 321-2025-001-00), the HPCI turbine stop valve (TSV) failed to open due to a degraded reset spring in the valve's trip knob assembly, caused by lack of scheduled preventive maintenance. At LER 387-2023-002-00, the HPCI Turbine Stop Valve failed to stroke fully closed during a Lube Oil System Functional Test, attributed to internal corrosion and mechanical binding of the valve's hydraulic drive mechanism from steam-related condensation. Note: LER 374-2021-001-00 concerns a High Pressure Core Spray (HPCS) water leg pump trip, not HPCI, so it is not included as an HPCI failure.

examples.question: Which events were mitigated by a redundant safety system being available?
examples.note: corpus-wide set of events with an available backup system (defense-in-depth) — a cross-document breadth query.

graph.answer: The evidence lists a large number of LERs where an event (e.g., reactor trip/scram, ESF actuation, component or train inoperability) was mitigated because a redundant or diverse safety system/train remained available. Examples include: LER 220-2020-001-01 (Nine Mile Point) — Control Room Air Treatment System inoperable, mitigated by Smoke Purge Removal; LER 237-2025-003-00 (Dresden) — HPCI inoperable, mitigated by BL and the Automatic Depressurization System; LER 244-2023-001-00 (Ginna) — EDG B inoperable, mitigated by EDG A; LER 254-2022-002-00 (Quad Cities) — both LPCI loops inoperable, mitigated by High Pressure ECCS and BM; LER 263-2022-001-00 (Monticello) — Control Room Envelope inoperable, mitigated by Control Room Emergency Filtration System; LER 296-2020-001-00 (Browns Ferry) — EDG actuation/partial loss of offsite power mitigated by DG; LER 298-2025-001-00 and 298-2026-001-00 (Cooper) — DG1 inoperable, mitigated by DG and Emergency/Startup Station Service Transformers; LER 321-2021-002-00 (Hatch) — 'B' LPCI loop inoperable, mitigated by BM and LPCI 'A' Loop; LER 338-2020-001-01 (North Anna) — 1J EDG inoperable, mitigated by 1H EDG; LER 366-2020-002-00 (Hatch) — HPCI and RCIC inoperable, mitigated by Low Pressure ECCS and Automatic Depressurization System; LER 346-2022-001-00 (Davis-Besse) — Decay Heat Pump 2/LPI Train 2 inoperable, mitigated by LPI Train 1/Decay Heat Pump 1; LER 413-2025-002-00 and 413-2025-003-00 (Catawba) — DG inoperable, mitigated by Emergency Supplemental Power Source, Safe-Shutdown Facility Diesel Generator (and FLEX equipment for the latter); LER 482-2020-002-00 (Wolf Creek) — 'B' EDG inoperable, mitigated by Offsite Power Sources and Station Blackout Diesel Generators; and numerous reactor trip/scram events across many plants (e.g., Turkey Point, Vogtle, Watts Bar, Beaver Valley, D.C. Cook, Farley, Comanche Peak, Palo Verde, South Texas, Waterford, McGuire, Prairie Island, Salem, Arkansas Nuclear, Seabrook) mitigated by Reactor Protection System actuation combined with Auxiliary/Emergency Feedwater System actuation or other backup trains (e.g., SJ, BA, SB, SG, EK, EJ, BP, JI, JL, AB). This is a broad, plant-wide pattern seen across essentially all listed events rather than isolated cases; the full list above enumerates each specific event and its associated redundant/backup system.

vector.answer: Based on the evidence, one clear case is LER 259-2024-003-00, where a breaker failure caused a valid actuation signal for the Emergency Diesel Generators (EDGs), which continued to power the affected Shutdown Boards (SD BDs) — i.e., the redundant EDG system was available and mitigated the event. Other retrieved LERs (e.g., 260-2023-001-01, 391-2024-002-00, 413-2020-003-00, 260-2025-003-01) state generally that sufficient/redundant systems were available and no safety systems were rendered inoperable, but they do not identify a specific failed component being backed up by a specific redundant system in the way 259-2024-003-00 does. LER 483-2020-002-01 describes a case where a backup positioner failed to assume control (so redundancy did NOT successfully mitigate), and LER 483-2025-001-00 discusses RWST inoperability where the guidance notes a report is required partly because 'no redundant equipment in the same system' was available, implying redundancy was not present or not confirmed in that instance. LER 445-2023-001-01 describes automatic actuation of the Auxiliary Feedwater System following a reactor trip, which is presented as the system responding as designed rather than a redundant backup system being invoked.

graph.answer: In LER 353-2025-001-00 (Limerick), the failure chain began with a degraded Cannon plug connector, which caused an electrical short circuit within the ECCS Contact Test Unit. This short circuit caused the HPCI Turbine Exhaust Line Vacuum Breaker Outboard Primary Containment Isolation Valve (PCIV) to close, which in turn rendered the HPCI System inoperable, resulting in a loss of its safety function. The stated cause category for this event is Design/Manufacturing/Installation. Backup systems available included trains BO, BM, BN, and the Automatic Depressurization System.

vector.answer: Several distinct HPCI events have occurred at Browns Ferry, each with a different cause: (1) In LER 259-2022-002-01, the Unit 1 HPCI system was declared inoperable due to a corroded actuator, attributed to procedural guidance in MPI-0-073-TRB001 being inadequate to ensure visual inspections identified adverse conditions before failure, and a maintenance strategy not aligned with industry best practices. (2) In LER 260-2024-002-01, Unit 2 HPCI was declared inoperable and isolated due to a rupture disc failure, discovered during a flowrate surveillance test when high rupture disc pressure indications occurred along with a HPCI turbine trip. (3) In LER 259-2026-001-00, Unit 1 HPCI was declared inoperable when steam line condensate drain valves failed closed due to a solenoid coil failure, most likely caused by thermal degradation of the coil's insulation. (4) In LER 260-2026-001-00, Unit 2 HPCI's steam line isolation valves isolated during a Steam Supply Low Pressure Functional Test, causing loss of the HPCI injection safety function (cause of the isolation itself is not detailed in the retrieved excerpt).
